summary: Sec 4.2 order_children throws std::overflow_error('integer length overflow') on a valid uint64 hierarchy from Algorithm 4 whose distances and masses all fit: the path of three edges of length ceil(2^64 / 5). The forest distance of Lemma 4.5 was accumulated as the signed pair (rd(a) + rd(b), 2 rd(lca)) of root distances of the link forest F; moving between the last two states adds 2q + 3q = 5q >= 2^64 although the distance is q. Root distances and their sums are auxiliary quantities, not path lengths. The reported inputs (path of four edges of 2^62 from vertex 2; lt::clustered(209953, 107) with bridges of 2^52 or more) also overflow the root distance itself and the Sec 4.1 mass.

found_by.test: P3-EVAL-ARITH-FIX: search for overflows of the same kind after saturating the Sec 4.1 mass (path 0-1-2-3-4 with four edges of 2^62, source 2); at the paper's size differential:Alg 4 Mode A + Evaluate at k = 209953: clustered, heavy uint64 bridges

fixed_by: fix(child-order): exact 128-bit forest distances and saturating gaps in Sec 4.2 [P3-CHILDORDER-OVERFLOW]
expected: the exact distances; root distances of F and the charge of Lemma 4.4 are formed in a 128-bit intermediate, and a gap that does not fit saturates at the infinity sentinel
